name: Chris Coons
stance: Wants mandatory public disclosure of AI model capabilities and safeguards, including against autonomous loss of control, enforced by the FTC.

statements.text: Americans cannot simply trust that technology companies will police themselves. When companies ask us to trust them, my response is simple: Show us.

Co-introduced the bipartisan AI Systems Transparency Act, requiring AI companies to disclose data practices and safeguards for child safety, cybersecurity, disaster risk and autonomous loss of control.
Companies must not be allowed to hand wave away these doubts without meaningful disclosures, safeguards, and oversight.
Americans deserve transparency from AI companies about what they’re doing to place safety guardrails on their models. I’ve got a bipartisan bill to do just that.
America and China are racing each other off a cliff. AI doesn’t care who wins. President Trump and President Xi need to find common ground on guardrails for AI before it gets ahead of us.

Calling Americans worried about the existential risks posed by AI "treasonists" and "traitors" is further proof President Trump doesn't understand the current moment. This White House isn't going to put meaningful guardrails on AI. Congress must.

It's time for the Trump Administration wake up to the existential threat posed by AI. This must be top of the agenda when Trump and Xi meet later this month, and Congress must prioritize passing meaningful guardrails in this space before it's too late.
Introduced a bill with Sen. Jack Reed to require human oversight of military AI, especially for nuclear weapons and domestic surveillance.

I’m encouraged by Anthropic’s launch of Project Glasswing, a coalition of America’s leading technology companies working together to deploy cutting-edge AI models to find and fix dangerous security flaws before our adversaries can exploit them.

Co-signed letters to OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Anthropic, Meta, Luka, Character.AI and xAI asking them to commit to timely, consistent safety disclosures around model releases, warning that trouble with well-understood risks raises concerns about managing more complex ones.

Joined a statement by eight Democratic senators objecting to the decision to allow Nvidia H200 AI chip exports to China, warning the chips would make China's weapons more lethal and its cyberattacks more effective.
